title: Navigating Metastatic Melanoma
summary: Learn how stage 4 melanoma survivor Steve navigates life, mentors newly diagnosed patients, and empowers others through self-advocacy and support resources.
body_markdown:
But as an adult he wore sunscreen, visited the dermatologist annually and knew what to look out for in terms of irregular moles. While nearly 90% of cutaneous (or, of the skin) melanoma cases can be linked to exposure to ultraviolet (UV) rays like the sun, it is not the only cause. Family history, genetics and other environmental factors can also contribute.1


Melanoma that is detected early — before it spreads beyond the skin — can often be treated successfully, with five-year survival rates exceeding 99%. However, when melanoma spreads to distant parts of the body, treatment can become more difficult. In these cases, the five-year survival rate drops to 35%, underscoring the importance of awareness, early detection and advances in care.2
